articles.title: Three PRs to Rowboat in 24 Hours, One of Them Taught Me More Than the Others
articles.excerpt: Last month I wrote about how I use coding agents to build things. This week I pointed the same setup at someone else's codebase. Rowboat (rowboatlabs/rowboat, 17.5k stars) had its good first issues pi…
articles.body: Last month I wrote about how I use coding agents to build things. This week I pointed the same setup at someone else's codebase. Rowboat (rowboatlabs/rowboat, 17.5k stars) had its good first issues picked clean, so I had to work for it a little. What I shipped Three pull requests in about a day: PR #1031: the sidebar Meetings subtitle showed an all-day event next week as if it happened today, masking a timed event that was sooner. Root cause was a sort that put all-day events first regardless of date, duplicated in two components. Fix: sort purely by start time, and give future all-day events a date qualifier so they never read as today. PR #1032: in child mode, if the spawned rowboat-server died, the app just logged it and the UI went stale.
articles.author: Kiell Tampubolon

articles.title: CCTP V1 vs V2: The Nonce Mismatch That Breaks Cross-Chain Arrival Checks
articles.excerpt: CCTP V1 vs V2: The Nonce Mismatch That Breaks Cross-Chain Arrival Checks While building a cross-chain transaction tracker on Base, I hit a subtle gotcha in Circle's CCTP (Cross-Chain Transfer Protocol…
articles.body: CCTP V1 vs V2: The Nonce Mismatch That Breaks Cross-Chain Arrival Checks While building a cross-chain transaction tracker on Base, I hit a subtle gotcha in Circle's CCTP (Cross-Chain Transfer Protocol) that took me a while to figure out. If you're building anything that tracks "did my USDC bridge transfer arrive on the destination chain?", this will save you a few hours. The Goal: Check If a Transfer Arrived The obvious way to verify a CCTP transfer completed is: On the source chain, decode the DepositForBurn event to get the deposit's nonce On the destination chain, query MessageTransmitter.usedNonces(...) - if the nonce is marked used, the transfer arrived Simple, right? That's exactly what the docs imply. It's also wrong.
articles.author: Lake Sky

articles.body: Turn your existing hardware into your own private AI server. Running AI locally can involve configuring runtimes, selecting compatible models, managing inference, and exposing APIs.

articles.title: 62 Years Later, Clint Eastwood's Genre-Redefining Western Is Officially Free on Streaming
articles.excerpt: The 1964 Spaghetti Western A Fistful of Dollars is availble for free on Youtube. Catch the genre-redefining film that made Clint Eastwood a star
articles.body: As the glory days of classic Westerns began to fade in the 1960s, so did some of the romance associated with it, bringing about the more complex, morally ambiguous “Revisionist Westerns.” One of the most important films from the early days of the Revisionist Western is 1964’s A Fistful of Dollars starring Clint Eastwood in his first major film role. It’s directed by Italian filmmaker Sergio Leone. A Fistful of Dollars is currently available for free on YouTube and is a can’t-miss for film fans — even those that aren’t so into Westerns. That’s mainly because A Fistful of Dollars is also a solid crime and action story that just so happens to take place in the Old West.

articles.title: I've chased the 'false dawn' for years — this is the week to find and photograph it
articles.excerpt: September's new moon opens a dark window for seeing zodiacal light, the ghostly cone of interplanetary dust that rises above the eastern horizon before dawn.
articles.body: Some stargazing feels like you know exactly what you are looking for, but you're still slightly unsure whether you are actually seeing it. Zodiacal light — meaning "light from the circle of animals" — is often like that. I have chased this so-called "false dawn" for years, and the first few minutes are always the same. I stare toward the horizon and wonder whether the sky is genuinely brighter there, or whether I am simply seeing distant light pollution, the first hint of morning twilight, or something my eyes have invented because I badly want to see it. However, under a genuinely dark sky — and particularly in a long-exposure image — its cone shape becomes obvious. Zodiacal light is enormous. It appears as a broad, softly glowing pyramid rising from the horizon.
